task 5: from 1000px, the header and footer span the page and the gear checklist sits beside the trails

cleanup.notes: Setup (npm ci in starter/) creates starter/node_modules, which holds Playwright 1.55.1 and the headless Chromium it downloads once (PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0 keeps the browser inside the lab folder). Cleanup deletes starter/node_modules; the tests create nothing else. Resetting the learner's work means copying starter/index.html and starter/styles.css back from a fresh copy of the lab (starter/badge.svg is never edited). The expected output file writes the variable timings as <ms>. The 60-minute cap is a planning allowance inside the 62 minutes of S21 Guided lab the intake assigns this lab, and the 53-minute median is a task-by-task authoring estimate of README reading plus the complete required task set: about 5 minutes to read the README, about 28 minutes for tasks 1 to 6 (single-rule CSS edits with TODO markers inline), about 12 minutes for tasks 7 to 10 (single-element markup fixes, each marked by a TODO task comment in index.html) and about 8 minutes for task 11 (box-model padding, border, margin and two calculated widths on two existing tags, taught on the S20 Concept day). The one-time setup (npm ci with its Chromium download) is done before the block and is not counted. Every task is required; there are no stretch tasks. Neither number is a measured learner pilot. Tasks 1 to 3 check the stated layout rules in the source files; tasks 4 and 5 also measure rendered outcomes in the pinned headless Chromium at breakpoint boundaries and the documented 700px and 1100px widths; task 6 measures overflow and hero fit at 400px; tasks 7 to 10 check the sign-up corner's rendered DOM in the same pinned Chromium: section and heading outline, programmatic label association, built-in validation via checkValidity, alt text and a native focusable submit button; task 11 measures each pack tag where it sits in the gear checklist: padding, border, bottom margin, zero side margins, box-sizing, and both its layout width and rendered border-box width with the checklist's own width fixed at two different sizes in each of two window sizes that differ in width and height, checking box-sizing in every case, with transitions on the checklist and the two tags switched off only while measuring and finite animations on them finished first, while an animation still running is read at one moment. It rejects a non-identity transform, scale, rotate, translate or zoom on the checklist itself or on a tag; an identity value counts only when it is static or the held end of a finished animation, and while an animation is still running on the element only none and 1 count. It measures at one moment: it first finishes the finite animations on the checklist and the two tags, so each of those then shows only what it holds after the animation (its last keyframe if it fills forwards, otherwise its unanimated values), and it reads every other animation, on any element, as it is at that moment. Any animation that changes the drawn size at some other moment can therefore go undetected. Examples include a paused, delayed or very long animation that does not hold its effect after it ends, an endless animation (for example one changing a width or padding, resting at none for part of each cycle, or pulsing the checklist's zoom), any animation on an element around the checklist, and animated custom properties. So the README asks learners to keep the assessed checklist layout, including layout-affecting motion around it, static. As a control it removes each tag's own width, min-width and max-width for a moment and requires the tag then to fill the checklist, so the 200px must come from the tag's own width. The README lists additional browser checks the learner does by hand.
